item.title: Correction · Pier 70 Parcel E1: The 2026-10-06 entry for this record said the 2033 date comes from…
item.description: The 2026-10-06 entry for this record said the 2033 date comes from the Development Agreement's Schedule of Performance. That was wrong. The Port's 2017 staff report (Item 9B, p.7) puts the Schedule of Performance in the Disposition and Development Agreement (DDA) between the Port and the developer, which is a different agreement from the Development Agreement between the City and the developer. The report says the developer must complete phase 2 within 16 years of project approval, but it never states the year 2033; 2033 is Pier & Point's own arithmetic (2017 plus 16 years). It stays labelled a legal outside date, not an expected completion. Source: https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Item%209B%20Pier%2070%20Approval%20092217.pdf.
item.source: https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Item%209B%20Pier%2070%20Approval%20092217.pdf

item.title: Correction · Pier 70 Parcel E1: The 2033 date shown for Parcel E1 is Pier & Point's arithmetic for…
item.description: The 2033 date shown for Parcel E1 is Pier & Point's arithmetic for the second-phase outside date in the Disposition and Development Agreement (DDA)'s Schedule of Performance, which is separate from the City's Development Agreement. The Port's report suggests but does not state that E1 is a Phase 2 parcel. It remains labelled a legal outside date, not a forecast. Source: Port of San Francisco, Item 9B: Pier 70 Mixed-Use Project approvals, Sep 22, 2017 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Item%209B%20Pier%2070%20Approval%20092217.pdf); Port of San Francisco, Item 11A: Pier 70 28-Acre Site Project update, Aug 7, 2026 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/2026-08/item_11a_p70_project_update_-_term_sheet_overview_-_information.pdf).

item.title: Correction · Pier 70 Parcel E1: We reworded several lines on the E1 page to match the Port's own…
item.description: We reworded several lines on the E1 page to match the Port's own documents: the 2017 approvals, the 2022 construction stall, when amendments are expected, and what the 2033 outside date covers. The 2017 estimate of about 143,000 gross square feet for E1 is now noted as a tax estimate, not a design. Source: Port Commission minutes, 2017-09-26 (sfport.com/media/2994/download?inline); The Real Deal, 2022-04-27 (therealdeal.com/san-francisco/2022/04/27/brookfield-pauses-3-5b-mixed-use-project-on-pier-70/); Bisnow, 2022-10-20 (bisnow.com/san-francisco/news/mixed-use/brookfield-properties-and-port-of-san-francisco-inch-closer-to-pier-70-completion-115959); Port Item 11A staff report, 2026-08-07 (sfport.com/sites/default/files/2026-08/item_11a_p70_project_update_-_term_sheet_overview_-_information.pdf); Port Item 12B memo, 2020-02-07, and Port Commission minutes, 2020-02-25 (sfport.com/media/5772/download?inline); Ordinance 224-17 (sfbos.org/sites/default/files/o0224-17.pdf); Port Item 9B staff report, 2017-09-22 (sfport.com/sites/default/files/Item%209B%20Pier%2070%20Approval%20092217.pdf); SF YIMBY, 2021-10-27 (sfyimby.com/2021/10/new-renderings-for-parcel-a-development-agreement-filed-for-pier-70-san-francisco.html).

item.title: Correction · Pier 70 Parcel E1: The 2033 date on this record was drawn as an expected completion
item.description: The 2033 date on this record was drawn as an expected completion. The Port's 2017 staff report calls it an outside date in the Development Agreement's Schedule of Performance (Phase 2 within 16 years of approval), not a construction schedule. It is now labelled a legal deadline and no longer moves this record's status on the map or the timeline. Source: https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Item%209B%20Pier%2070%20Approval%20092217.pdf.
item.source: https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Item%209B%20Pier%2070%20Approval%20092217.pdf

item.title: Correction · Pier 70 Parcel E1: The 2033 completion milestone is now labelled a soft 2017 outside…
item.description: The 2033 completion milestone is now labelled a soft 2017 outside date that down market delay has tolled and Port Item 11A proposes to reset, not a current expectation. The Item 11A milestone is dated to the Aug 7, 2026 staff report rather than as a hearing that took place. Image credits no longer say 'adopted 2017' or give an unstated Aug 11 meeting date, and the SUD land-use plan credit now notes the SITELAB logo on the sheet. The map notes cite the Port for current status and no longer claim the site was never subdivided by the Assessor. The D4D source is no longer called an 'adopted' document, and the Mayor's signing entry now states the Board of Supervisors' first-reading vote on Oct 31, 2017 and final passage on Nov 14, 2017. Source: Port of San Francisco, Commission Item 11A staff report, 2026-08-07 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/2026-08/item_11a_p70_project_update_-_term_sheet_overview_-_information.pdf); Port of San Francisco, Commission Item 9B staff report, 2017-09-22 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Item%209B%20Pier%2070%20Approval%20092217.pdf); Port of San Francisco, Pier 70 SUD Land Use Plan, 2018-03-13 (https://sfport.com/files/2021-11/pier_70_sud_land_use_plan.pdf); Port of San Francisco, Pier 70 Special Use District Design for Development, updated 2022-04-26 (https://www.sfport.com/media/8123/download?inline=); San Francisco Board of Supervisors, Ordinance No. 224-17 (https://sfbos.org/sites/default/files/o0224-17.pdf).
item.source: Port of San Francisco, Commission Item 11A staff report, 2026-08-07 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/2026-08/item_11a_p70_project_update_-_term_sheet_overview_-_information.pdf); Port of San Francisco, Commission Item 9B staff report, 2017-09-22 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Item%209B%20Pier%2070%20Approval%20092217.pdf); Port of San Francisco, Pier 70 SUD Land Use Plan, 2018-03-13 (https://sfport.com/files/2021-11/pier_70_sud_land_use_plan.pdf); Port of San Francisco, Pier 70 Special Use District Design for Development, updated 2022-04-26 (https://www.sfport.com/media/8123/download?inline=); San Francisco Board of Supervisors, Ordinance No. 224-17 (https://sfbos.org/sites/default/files/o0224-17.pdf)

item.title: Milestone · Pier 70 Parcel E1: Port staff report (memo dated Aug 7, 2026) for the… (Aug 7, 2026)
item.description: Port staff report (memo dated Aug 7, 2026) for the Aug 11, 2026 Port Commission meeting (informational item 11A) describes proposed DDA amendments: parcel-specific outside dates, a Project-wide affordable rate of no less than 20% (327 stand-alone affordable units kept), 65-to-90 ft height increases on certain residential parcels, developer return cut from 18% to 14%, and a new phasing plan (Aug 7, 2026). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07; Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-11.
item.source: Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07; Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-11

item.title: Expected · Pier 70 Parcel E1: Port Commission: Port staff and the developer are… (~Dec 2026)
item.description: Port Commission: Port staff and the developer are drafting amendments to the DDA and related transaction documents "for consideration by the Port Commission and Board of Supervisors by the end of this year or early next year" (Item 11A, memo of Aug 7, 2026, p.2 and p.6). The source gives no hearing date. The date shown is the early end of that window (December 2026); "early next year" falls in 2027. The same report proposes extending the term of the DDA, Development Agreement and Master Lease by 5 years. (~Dec 2026). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07.
item.source: Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07

item.title: Expected · Pier 70 Parcel E1: Then the Board of Supervisors: the same amendments are… (~Dec 2026)
item.description: Then the Board of Supervisors: the same amendments are to go to the Board of Supervisors in the same window (Item 11A, p.6: "for consideration by the Port Commission and Board of Supervisors by the end of this year or early next year"). The source gives no separate date or order for the Board. The date shown is the early end of the window; "early next year" falls in 2027. (~Dec 2026). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07.
item.source: Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07

item.title: Expected · Pier 70 Parcel E1: The Phase 1 down market delay, which tolls the… (Dec 26, 2026)
item.description: The Phase 1 down market delay, which tolls the developer's time-sensitive DDA obligations including close of escrow on option parcels, is extended to December 26, 2026: it reached its 60-month maximum in June 2026 and the parties agreed to extend it six months to allow time to complete the DDA amendments (Item 11A, memo of Aug 7, 2026, p.4: "the parties mutually agreed to extend the down market delay for an additional six months to December 26, 2026"). This is the end date of an extension the parties agreed under the DDA; the report does not call it a deadline, and it is not a forecast. (Dec 26, 2026). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07.
item.source: Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07

item.title: Expected · Pier 70 Parcel E1: The DDA's Schedule of Performance sets an outside date for… (~2033)
item.description: The DDA's Schedule of Performance sets an outside date for completing Phase 2 at 16 years after Project approval; Item 9B describes these outside dates as covering 'horizontal improvements for each phase' and related public benefits, so this is not a completion date for a building on E1; Pier & Point's arithmetic from 2017 gives about 2033 (the Port's report states no calendar year). Item 9B does not list parcels by phase; its Table A ties a Phase 2 benefit (Building 21) to this parcel's temporary certificate of occupancy, which suggests but does not state that E1 is a Phase 2 parcel. Not a current forecast for this parcel, which the Port's proposed 2026 phasing plan groups with E4 and Building 21 in subphase 2C (~2033). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2017-09-22; Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07.
item.source: Port of San Francisco, 2017-09-22; Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07

item.title: Milestone · Pier 70 Parcel E1: Brookfield halts construction on the 28-Acre Site: The… (~Apr 2022)
item.description: Brookfield halts construction on the 28-Acre Site: The Real Deal (Apr 27, 2022, citing the San Francisco Business Times) reports 'Brookfield has halted construction' because of economic conditions, and Bisnow (Oct 20, 2022) reports that after the first phase's infrastructure and roadwork were completed 'progress stalled in April, with officials citing market conditions'. The Port's Aug 2026 report says the balance of Phase 1 horizontal work, largely the parks, is still to be built, so this was not the end of all Phase 1 horizontal work (~Apr 2022). Source: The Real Deal (citing San Francisco Business Times), 2022-04-27; Bisnow (Joseph Gordon), 2022-10-20; The Real Deal (citing SF Business Times), 2023-04-17; Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07.
item.source: The Real Deal (citing San Francisco Business Times), 2022-04-27; Bisnow (Joseph Gordon), 2022-10-20; The Real Deal (citing SF Business Times), 2023-04-17; Port of San Francisco, 2026-08-07
